speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long this lesion has been present and if you recall any specific injury to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The combination of an ulcerative lesion appearing at a site of trauma (ant bite), your history of Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes, and recent use of corticosteroids for anterior uveitis strongly suggests this diagnosis. I will not request further tests or images as the clinical picture is sufficient for management; we will proceed with systemic immunosuppression.
